Pablo-

If you visited the transect 4 times, you should enter each transect as a si=
ngle sample record and the value of the effort should be 4 times the length=
of the transect, if this is line transect data. If it is point data then =
the effort should be entered as 4 for each point. Unless you misstated the =
comparison of old and new below, this will not help resolve the differences=
because this will reduce the density of your current survey if you entered=
the sightings from all 4 visits but only entered the effort as 1 times the=
length of the line.

--jeff

On Wed, Aug 29, 2012 at 1:08 PM, Oleiro, Pablo C. (MU-Student) <pablo.oleir=
o...@mail.missouri.edu<mailto:pablo....@mail.missouri.edu>> wrote:
Dear Distance Community,

Like Jessica I am comparing my bird survey for Pohnpei data to old data ga=
ther by the USFS. Also I am repeatig the same transect and general areas th=
at they did in the 80. In previous studies they just visit each transect on=
ce , I visit the transects 4 times which gave me a larger number of detecti=
ons. Old studies and my study have similar detection probabilities values a=
nd our numbers of detections are similar as well. But density values for th=
e old study are much higher than my study. I believe that is because I do n=
ot know how to account for the fact that I have 4 visits to each transect.
If I need to upload my data in another way
Where are the steps to account for my 4 visits
Is Ok or not if just use an average of my visits?
I would appreciate any input and experiences that you may have with a simil=
ar issue.

Thank you very much,

Sincerely

Pablo C. Oleiro

Sent: Wednesday, August 22, 2012 5:38 AM
To: DISTANCE...@JISCMAIL.AC.UK<mailto:DISTANCE...@JISCMAIL.AC.U=
K>
Subject: [DIST-SAMP] Setting up project with transects used multiple times

Hi all,
I would be very grateful for some advice on setting up my data in Distance.=
I have done 4 counts (2 summer, 2 winter over 1 yr) of bustards on a total=
of about 4500 km of roads in South Africa. I realise the issues with using=
roads, but I am repeating the methodology of surveys done exactly this way=
in the 1980s (the routes only differ in the current surveys slightly where=
roads became impassable in places etc), and I have some satellite tracking=
data which I am hoping will support my theory that these birds do not avoi=
d roads. The route is mostly continuous, and goes through 18 different bior=
egions. In the 1980s, 4 surveys were done, but distance measurements were o=
nly made on 1 survey. There is a strong seasonal effect (lots of birds in w=
inter, not in summer), so I will focus on winter counts.
The overall aims of the research are to see if there has been a population =
decline and to estimate a current population (which I was planning to do st=
ratified by bioregion). So I have set up my project using bioregion as regi=
on, the 5 surveys (4 of mine and 1 historic) as line transects (the amount =
of road travelled in each bioregion), and then the sighting data as observa=
tions. Using the data filters I am planning to come up with an density for =
just the historic survey, and then a current one (using my winter data).
I am just a bit concerned that the line transects in each season are the sa=
me and not independent, so I wondered if I have set this up in the appropri=
ate way? I looked at multipliers but I don't think I can use these and stil=
l keep the season data?
Many thanks
Jessica
